verses.text: Trouble is coming for people who pass crooked laws and write rules that crush others,
taking justice away from people in need and stealing the rights of the poor among my people, so they can rob widows and prey on children without fathers.
What will you do when the day of reckoning comes and disaster hits from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you stash your wealth?
You'll have nowhere to go but down among the prisoners or under the bodies of the dead. Even after all this, his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Trouble for Assyria, the rod of my anger! The staff in its hand carries my fury.
I'll send him against a nation that treats nothing as sacred. I'll order him to strip the people who make me angry, take what he wants, and trample them like mud in the street.
But that's not what he thinks he's doing. That's not the plan in his heart. What he wants is to wipe out nations, and plenty of them.
He says, “Aren't all my commanders kings?
Is Calno any different from Carchemish? Hamath from Arpad? Samaria from Damascus?”
My hand reached kingdoms full of idols, with carved images that outdid the ones in Jerusalem and Samaria.
Won't I do to Jerusalem and her idols exactly what I did to Samaria and hers?
When the Lord finishes everything he means to do on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he'll punish what grew out of the king of Assyria's stubborn pride and that arrogant look on his face.

The king said, “I did it with my own strength and my own wisdom. I know what I'm doing. I moved the borders of whole peoples and robbed their treasuries. I brought their rulers down like a mighty warrior.
I reached into a nest and found all the wealth of the peoples. I gathered up the whole earth the way you pick up abandoned eggs. Nobody flapped a wing, opened a mouth, or let out a chirp.”

Does an ax get to brag over the person swinging it? Does a saw get to act bigger than the person using it? That's like a rod picking up the person holding it, or a wooden staff lifting somebody who's no piece of wood.
That's why the Lord, GOD of Armies, will make his well-fed ones waste away. A blaze will catch under all his glory and burn like fire.
Israel's light will become a fire, and Israel's Holy One a flame. It'll burn through all his thorns and briers in a single day.
He'll burn up the glory of the forest and the rich fields, body and soul. It'll be like a flag bearer collapsing.
So few trees will be left in his forest that a child could write down the number.
That day those left of Israel and the people who escaped from Jacob's family won't lean on the one who struck them anymore. They'll truly lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will come back. Those left of Jacob will come back to the mighty God.
Israel, even if your people are as countless as sand by the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decided, and it will overflow with righteousness.
The Lord, GOD of Armies, will carry out the full destruction he's determined across the whole earth.
So the Lord, GOD of Armies, says, “My people who live in Zion, don't be scared of the Assyrian, even if he hits you with a rod and raises his staff against you like Egypt did.
In just a little while my anger against you will have run its course. Then I'll turn my anger on him to destroy him.”
The LORD of Armies will raise a whip against him, like when Midian was slaughtered at the rock of Oreb. His rod will reach over the sea, and he'll raise it like he did against Egypt.
That day his load will come off your shoulders and his yoke off your neck. The yoke will break because of the anointing oil.
He's reached Aiath and passed through Migron. He's storing his baggage at Michmash.
They've crossed the pass and stopped for the night at Geba. Ramah is shaking. Saul's Gibeah has run away.
Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is on the run. The people of Gebim are fleeing to safety.
Today he'll stop at Nob and shake his fist at the mountain of daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord, GOD of Armies, will chop off the branches with terrifying force. The tall ones will be cut down, and the ones that tower overhead will come low.
He'll hack through the thick forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall at the hand of the Mighty One.
